sentences.chinese: 姚興
sentences.literal: Yao Xing
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing

sentences.literal: (Part One)
sentences.idiomatic: (Part One)

sentences.chinese: 姚興，字子略，萇之長子也。
sentences.literal: Yao Xing, styled Zilüe, was the eldest son of Yao Chang.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing, whose courtesy name was Zilüe, was the eldest son of Yao Chang.

sentences.chinese: 苻堅時為太子舍人。
sentences.literal: Under Fu Jian he served as Gentleman Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
sentences.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's reign he held the office of Gentleman Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.chinese: 萇之在馬牧，興自長安冒難奔萇，萇立為皇太子。
sentences.literal: When Chang was at the Horse Pastures, Xing braved danger from Chang'an to flee to Chang, and Chang established him as imperial heir apparent.
sentences.idiomatic: While Yao Chang was stationed at the Horse Pastures, Yao Xing braved peril to flee from Chang'an and join him, and Yao Chang installed him as crown prince.

sentences.chinese: 萇出征討，常留統後事。
sentences.literal: Whenever Chang went out on campaign, he always left Xing behind to oversee rear affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: Whenever Yao Chang marched on campaign, he routinely left Yao Xing behind to manage affairs in the rear.

sentences.chinese: 及鎮長安，甚有威惠。
sentences.literal: When he garrisoned Chang'an, he was greatly awe-inspiring and beneficent.
sentences.idiomatic: When he held Chang'an, he ruled with both stern authority and kindness.

sentences.chinese: 與其中舍人梁喜、洗馬範勖等講論經籍，不以兵難廢業，時人咸化之。
sentences.literal: With Palace Gentleman Liang Xi, Groom Fan Xu, and others he discussed the classics; he did not abandon study because of military troubles; people of the time were all transformed by him.
sentences.idiomatic: He debated the classics with Liang Xi, Gentleman of the Palace Within, Fan Xu, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and others, refusing to abandon scholarship because of the hardships of war; his contemporaries took inspiration from him.

sentences.chinese: 萇死，興秘不發喪，以其叔父緒鎮安定，碩德鎮陰密，弟崇守長安。
sentences.literal: When Chang died, Xing kept it secret and did not announce mourning; he had his uncle Xu garrison Anding, Shuode garrison Yinmi, and younger brother Chong defend Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died, Yao Xing concealed the death and withheld the obsequies; he assigned his uncle Yao Xu to hold Anding, Yao Shuode to hold Yinmi, and his younger brother Yao Chong to defend Chang'an.

sentences.chinese: 碩德將佐言於碩德曰：「公威名宿重，部曲最強，今喪代之際，朝廷必相猜忌，非永安之道也。
sentences.literal: Shuode's generals and aides said to Shuode: "Your lordship's fearsome name is long established and your personal troops are the strongest; now at the juncture of succession the court is sure to turn suspicious; this is no way to lasting security.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuode's subordinates said to him: "Your prestige has stood for years and your command is the strongest force at hand; at a moment of imperial succession the court will inevitably grow wary of you; that is no path to lasting peace.

sentences.chinese: 宜奔秦州，觀望事勢。
sentences.literal: You ought to flee to Qinzhou and watch how circumstances develop.
sentences.idiomatic: You should withdraw to Qinzhou and see how the situation unfolds.

sentences.chinese: 」碩德曰：「太子志度寬明，必無疑阻。
sentences.literal: " Shuode said: "The heir apparent's mind is generous and clear; there will surely be no suspicion or obstruction.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuode replied: "The crown prince is broad-minded and discerning; he will not harbor groundless doubts or block our way.

sentences.chinese: 今苻登未滅而自尋干戈，所謂追二袁之蹤，授首與人。
sentences.literal: Now Fu Deng is not yet destroyed yet we would seek strife among ourselves—what is called following in the footsteps of the two Yuans and handing our heads to another.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng still lives; if we now turn our blades on one another, we shall only repeat the folly of the two Yuans and hand victory to someone else.

sentences.chinese: 吾死而已，終不若斯。
sentences.literal: I would rather die; I will never be like that.
sentences.idiomatic: I would sooner die than follow such counsel.

sentences.chinese: 」及至，興優禮而遣之。
sentences.literal: When he arrived, Xing treated him with exceptional courtesy and sent him away.
sentences.idiomatic: When Yao Shuode arrived, Yao Xing received him with exceptional courtesy and let him return to his post.

sentences.chinese: 興自稱大將軍，以尹緯為長史，狄伯支為司馬，率眾伐苻登。
sentences.literal: Xing styled himself Grand General; he appointed Yin Wei as Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi as Marshal, and led the host to attack Fu Deng.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing took the title of Grand General, appointed Yin Wei as Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi as Marshal, and led the army against Fu Deng.

sentences.chinese: 咸陽太守劉忌奴據避世堡以叛，興襲忌奴，擒之。
sentences.literal: The Administrator of Xianyang Liu Jinu occupied Bishibao and rebelled; Xing attacked Jinu and captured him.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Jinu, Administrator of Xianyang, seized Bishibao and rose in rebellion; Yao Xing struck him, took him prisoner, and subdued the revolt.

sentences.chinese: 苻登自六陌向廢橋，始平太守姚詳據馬嵬堡以距登。
sentences.literal: Fu Deng advanced from Liumo toward Feiqiao; the Administrator of Shiping Yao Xiang held Maweibao to resist Deng.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched from Liumo toward Feiqiao; Yao Xiang, Administrator of Shiping, entrenched himself at Maweibao to hold Fu Deng at bay.

sentences.chinese: 登眾甚盛，興慮詳不能遏，乃自將精騎以迫登，遣尹緯領步卒赴詳。
sentences.literal: Deng's forces were very strong; Xing worried Xiang could not stop them, so he personally led picked cavalry to press Deng and sent Yin Wei to lead infantry to reinforce Xiang.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng's army was formidable; Yao Xing feared Yao Xiang could not contain it, so he personally led elite horsemen to pressure Fu Deng while dispatching Yin Wei with foot soldiers to reinforce Yao Xiang.

sentences.chinese: 緯用詳計，據廢橋以抗登。
sentences.literal: Wei adopted Xiang's plan and held Feiqiao to resist Deng.
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei followed Yao Xiang's plan and secured Feiqiao to block Fu Deng.

sentences.chinese: 登因急攻緯，緯將出戰，興馳遣狄伯支謂緯曰：「兵法不戰而制人者，蓋為此也。
sentences.literal: Deng therefore pressed the attack on Wei; Wei was about to go out to fight when Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei: "The art of war's 'subdue others without fighting'—this is surely what it means.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng redoubled his assault on Yin Wei; as Yin Wei was about to give battle, Yao Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi with orders: "The maxim that the adept warrior wins without fighting is meant for moments such as this.

sentences.chinese: 苻登窮寇，宜持重，不可輕戰。
sentences.literal: Fu Deng is a cornered bandit; you should hold firm and must not fight lightly.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng is a desperate foe; stand firm and do not hazard a rash engagement.

sentences.chinese: 」緯曰：「先帝登遐，人情擾懼，今不因思奮之力，梟殄逆豎，大事去矣。
sentences.literal: " Wei said: "The late emperor has ascended on high; men's hearts are disturbed and afraid; if we do not now rely on the power of those who yearn to strive and behead and exterminate the rebellious villain, the great enterprise is lost.
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei answered: "The late sovereign has just passed away; fear and uncertainty grip the army. If we do not seize this surge of loyal resolve to strike down the traitor Fu Deng, the whole enterprise is lost.

sentences.chinese: 緯敢以死爭。
sentences.literal: Wei dares to contend with death.
sentences.idiomatic: I am prepared to stake my life on this battle.

sentences.chinese: 」遂與登戰，大破之，登眾渴死者十二三，其夜大潰，登奔雍。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he fought Deng and utterly defeated him; two or three men in ten of Deng's army died of thirst; that night they broke in great disorder; Deng fled to Yong.
sentences.idiomatic: He engaged Fu Deng and won a crushing victory; two or three men in ten of Fu Deng's army perished of thirst, and that night the enemy ranks collapsed in panic as Fu Deng fled toward Yong.

sentences.chinese: 興乃發喪行服。
sentences.literal: Xing then announced the mourning and observed mourning garments.
sentences.idiomatic: Only then did Yao Xing publicly announce his father's death and don mourning garb.

sentences.chinese: 太元十九年，僭即帝位於槐里，大赦境內，改元曰皇初，遂如安定。
sentences.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan, he usurped the imperial title at Huaili, issued a general amnesty within the realm, changed the era name to Huangchu, and then went to Anding.
sentences.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Jin Taiyuan era he presumptuously assumed the throne at Huaili, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout his realm, adopted the reign title Huangchu, and then proceeded to Anding.

sentences.chinese: 先是，苻登使弟廣守雍，子崇屯胡空堡，聞登敗，各棄守走。
sentences.literal: Earlier, Fu Deng had sent younger brother Guang to defend Yong and son Chong to encamp at Hukongbao; hearing of Deng's defeat, each abandoned his post and fled.
sentences.idiomatic: Earlier, Fu Deng had stationed his brother Fu Guang at Yong and his son Fu Chong at Hukongbao; when they heard of his defeat, both abandoned their positions and fled.

sentences.chinese: 登無所投據，遂奔平涼，率其餘眾入馬毛山。
sentences.literal: Deng had nowhere to turn; he fled to Pingliang and led his remaining host into Maomaoshan.
sentences.idiomatic: With no refuge left, Fu Deng rushed to Pingliang and led his surviving troops into the Maomao Hills.

sentences.chinese: 興自安定如涇陽，與登戰于山南，斬登。
sentences.literal: Xing went from Anding to Jingyang and fought Deng south of the mountain; he beheaded Deng.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched from Anding to Jingyang, fought Fu Deng south of the mountains, and slew him in the field.

sentences.chinese: 散其部眾，歸復農業。
sentences.literal: He dispersed Deng's troops and returned them to farming.
sentences.idiomatic: He disbanded Fu Deng's soldiers and sent them back to their fields.

sentences.chinese: 徙陰密三萬戶于長安，分大營戶為四，置四軍以領之。
sentences.literal: He moved thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, divided the great camp households into four, and established four armies to command them.
sentences.idiomatic: He relocated thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, split the former great camp population into four divisions, and created four armies to command them.

sentences.chinese: 安南強熙、鎮遠楊多叛，推竇沖為盟主，所在擾亂。
sentences.literal: Qiang Xi the Pacifier of the South and Yang Duo the Stabilizer of the Distance rebelled; they set up Dou Chong as covenant lord; everywhere was disturbed.
sentences.idiomatic: Qiang Xi, General Who Pacifies the South, and Yang Duo, General Who Stabilizes the Distance, rose in revolt and proclaimed Dou Chong their leader; unrest spread across the region.

sentences.chinese: 興率諸將討之，軍次武功，多兄子良國殺多而降。
sentences.literal: Xing led the generals to punish them; the army halted at Wugong; Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing led his commanders against them and camped at Wugong, where Yang Liangguo, Yang Duo's nephew, assassinated Yang Duo and came over to Yao Xing's side.

sentences.chinese: 沖弟彰武與沖離貳，沖奔強熙。
sentences.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhangwu fell out with Chong; Chong fled to Qiang Xi.
sentences.idiomatic: Dou Chong's younger brother Dou Zhangwu broke with him, so Dou Chong fled to join Qiang Xi.

sentences.chinese: 熙聞興將至，率戶二千奔秦州。
sentences.literal: Xi heard Xing was coming and led two thousand households to flee to Qinzhou.
sentences.idiomatic: When Qiang Xi learned that Yao Xing was approaching, he took two thousand households and fled toward Qinzhou.

sentences.chinese: 竇沖走汧川，汧川氐仇高執送之。
sentences.literal: Dou Chong fled to Qianchuan; the Di of Qianchuan Qiu Gao seized him and sent him in.
sentences.idiomatic: Dou Chong fled to Qianchuan, where Qiu Gao of the local Di people seized him and delivered him to the court.

sentences.chinese: 沖從弟統率其眾降於興。
sentences.literal: Chong's cousin Tong led his host to surrender to Xing.
sentences.idiomatic: Dou Chong's cousin Dou Tong led the remainder of the rebel forces to surrender to Yao Xing.

sentences.chinese: 封征虜緒為晉王，征西碩德為隴西王，征南靖等及功臣尹緯、齊難、楊佛嵩等並為公侯，其餘封爵各有差。
sentences.literal: He enfeoffed Xu the Subduer of Captives as Prince of Jin, Shuode the West Campaigner as Prince of Longxi, Jing the South Campaigner and others and meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others as dukes and marquises; the rest received enfeoffments of varying rank.
sentences.idiomatic: He invested Yao Xu, General Who Subdues Invaders, as Prince of Jin; Yao Shuode, General Who Campaigns West, as Prince of Longxi; Yao Jing, General Who Campaigns South, together with such merit holders as Yin Wei, Qi Nan, and Yang Fosong, received ducal or marquisal rank; other officers were ennobled according to their deeds.

sentences.chinese: 鮮卑薛勃於貳城為魏軍所伐，遣使請救，使姚崇赴救。
sentences.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo at Ercheng was attacked by Wei forces; he sent envoys asking for aid; Xing sent Yao Chong to relieve him.
sentences.idiomatic: The Xianbei leader Xue Bo, holding Ercheng, was attacked by Wei troops; he appealed for rescue, and Yao Xing sent Yao Chong to relieve him.

sentences.chinese: 魏師既還，薛勃復叛，崇伐而執之，大收其士馬而還。
sentences.literal: After the Wei army withdrew, Xue Bo rebelled again; Chong attacked and captured him, greatly collected his soldiers and horses, and returned.
sentences.idiomatic: After the Wei army withdrew, Xue Bo rebelled again; Yao Chong campaigned against him, took him captive, seized large numbers of men and mounts, and withdrew.

sentences.chinese: 興追尊其庶母孫氏為皇太后，配饗太廟。
sentences.literal: Xing posthumously honored his father's concubine Lady Sun as Empress Dowager and accorded her joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing posthumously elevated his father's concubine, Lady Sun, to Empress Dowager and granted her a place beside the royal ancestors in the Grand Temple.

sentences.chinese: 楊盛保仇池，遣使請命，拜使持節、鎮南將軍、仇池公。
sentences.literal: Yang Sheng held Qiuchi and sent envoys suing for appointment; he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Qiuchi.
sentences.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, who held Qiuchi, sent envoys suing for recognition; Yao Xing appointed him Bearer of the Imperial Staff, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.chinese: 鮮卑越質詰歸率戶二萬叛乞伏乾歸，降於興，興處之于成紀，拜使持節、鎮西將軍、平襄公。
sentences.literal: The Xianbei Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households to rebel against Qifu Gangui and surrender to Xing; Xing settled them at Chengji and appointed him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.
sentences.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households in breaking away from Qifu Gangui and submitting to Yao Xing; Yao Xing resettled them at Chengji and named him Bearer of the Imperial Staff, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.chinese: 姚碩德討平涼胡金豹於洛城，克之。
sentences.literal: Yao Shuode attacked the Pingliang Hu Jin Bao at Luocheng and took it.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuode campaigned against the Pingliang Hu leader Jin Bao at Luocheng and captured the town.

sentences.chinese: 初，上邽薑乳據本縣以叛，自稱秦州刺史。
sentences.literal: Earlier, Jiang Ru of Shanggui held his home county in rebellion and styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou.
sentences.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang Ru of Shanggui had seized his home county, rebelled, and declared himself Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.chinese: 碩德進討之，乳率眾降。
sentences.literal: Shuode advanced to attack him; Ru led his host to surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuode advanced against him; Jiang Ru led his forces in surrender.

sentences.chinese: 以碩德為秦州牧，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。
sentences.literal: He appointed Shuode as Governor of Qinzhou, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
sentences.idiomatic: He named Yao Shuode Governor of Qinzhou, with the additional post of Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and stationed him at Shanggui.

sentences.chinese: 征乳為尚書。
sentences.literal: He summoned Ru to serve as Minister.
sentences.idiomatic: He summoned Jiang Ru to the capital to serve as a Minister of State.

sentences.chinese: 強熙及略陽豪族權幹城率眾三萬圍上邽，碩德擊破之。
sentences.literal: Qiang Xi and the magnate of Lueyang Quan Gancheng led thirty thousand to besiege Shanggui; Shuode defeated them.
sentences.idiomatic: Qiang Xi and Quan Gancheng, a powerful clan leader from Lueyang, brought thirty thousand men to besiege Shanggui; Yao Shuode broke their army.

sentences.chinese: 熙南奔仇池，遂假道歸晉。
sentences.literal: Xi fled south to Qiuchi and then borrowed passage to return to Jin.
sentences.idiomatic: Qiang Xi fled south to Qiuchi and from there obtained safe conduct into Eastern Jin territory.

sentences.chinese: 碩德西討幹城，幹城降。
sentences.literal: Shuode campaigned west against Gancheng; Gancheng surrendered.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuode then marched west against Quan Gancheng, who capitulated.

sentences.chinese: 興令郡國各歲貢清行孝廉一人。
sentences.literal: Xing ordered each commandery and kingdom annually to recommend one pure-conduct filial and incorrupt candidate.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing decreed that every commandery and princedom should each year nominate one candidate for the Filial and Incorrupt examination who excelled in moral conduct.

sentences.chinese: 慕容永既為慕容垂所滅，河東太守柳恭等各阻兵自守，興遣姚緒討之。
sentences.literal: After Murong Yong had been destroyed by Murong Chui, the Administrators of Hedong Liu Gong and others each held troops and defended themselves; Xing sent Yao Xu to attack them.
sentences.idiomatic: After Murong Chui had destroyed Murong Yong, regional administrators such as Liu Gong of Hedong dug in with their own troops; Yao Xing dispatched Yao Xu to reduce them.

sentences.chinese: 恭等依河距守，緒不得濟。
sentences.literal: Gong and the others relied on the river to defend; Xu could not cross.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Gong and his allies held the Yellow River line, and Yao Xu could not force a crossing.

sentences.chinese: 鎮東薛強先據楊氏壁，引緒從龍門濟河，遂入蒲阪。
sentences.literal: Xue Qiang the East Stabilizer first held Yangshi Stockade and guided Xu from Longmen to cross the river; thereupon they entered Puban.
sentences.idiomatic: Xue Qiang, the general holding the east, had already occupied Yangshi Stockade; he guided Yao Xu across the river at Longmen, and the army entered Puban.

sentences.chinese: 恭勢屈，請降。
sentences.literal: Gong's situation gave way and he asked to surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: Seeing his position collapse, Liu Gong offered his surrender.

sentences.chinese: 徙新平、安定新戶六千于蒲阪。
sentences.literal: He moved six thousand new households from Xinping and Anding to Puban.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing resettled six thousand newly registered households from Xinping and Anding in Puban.

sentences.chinese: 興母虵氏死，興哀毀過禮，不親庶政。
sentences.literal: Xing's mother Lady She died; Xing's grief wasted him beyond the rites and he did not personally attend to routine government.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing's mother, Lady She, died; he mourned so fiercely that he exceeded prescribed ritual and ceased to handle daily affairs of state.

sentences.chinese: 群臣議請依漢、魏故事，既葬即吉。
sentences.literal: The ministers deliberated and asked to follow Han and Wei precedent—after burial return to auspicious dress at once.
sentences.idiomatic: His ministers debated the matter and urged him to follow Han and Wei precedent by ending mourning as soon as the burial was complete.

sentences.chinese: 興尚書郎李嵩上疏曰「三王異制，五帝殊禮。
sentences.literal: Li Song, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial saying: "The Three Kings had differing systems; the Five Emperors had diverse rites.
sentences.idiomatic: Li Song, a Gentleman at the Masters of Writing, presented a memorial: "The Three Ages knew variant institutions; the Five Emperors observed differing rites.

sentences.chinese: 孝治天下，先王之高事也，宜遵聖性，以光道訓。
sentences.literal: Filial piety rules the realm—it is the supreme affair of the former kings; one ought to follow sagely nature to brighten the way of instruction.
sentences.idiomatic: Governing the world through filial devotion was the highest priority of the ancient sages; Your Majesty should heed your own humane nature and thereby illuminate moral teaching.

sentences.chinese: 既葬之後，應素服臨朝，率先天下，仁孝之舉也。
sentences.literal: After burial, plain garments should attend court, leading all under Heaven—it is an act of benevolent filial piety.
sentences.idiomatic: After the interment you should hold court in plain hemp, setting an example for the realm—such is the conduct of humane filial piety.

sentences.chinese: 」尹緯駁曰：「帝王喪制，漢、魏為准。
sentences.literal: " Yin Wei refuted: "For imperial mourning regulations, Han and Wei are the standard.
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei objected: "Imperial mourning law takes the Han and Wei codes as its touchstone.

sentences.chinese: 嵩矯常越禮，愆於軌度，請付有司，以專擅論。
sentences.literal: Song bends the norm and oversteps ritual; he errs against measure—please hand him to the authorities for judgment on presumption.
sentences.idiomatic: Li Song twists convention and oversteps ritual propriety; he departs from proper bounds. Hand him to the judicial officials and try him for overstepping authority.

sentences.chinese: 既葬即吉，乞依前議。
sentences.literal: After burial return to auspicious dress—we beg to follow the earlier deliberation.
sentences.idiomatic: End mourning when the burial is finished; we respectfully ask that you adhere to the ministers' original proposal.

sentences.chinese: 」興曰：「嵩忠臣孝子，有何咎乎？
sentences.literal: " Xing said: "Song is a loyal minister and filial son—what fault is there?
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing said: "Li Song speaks as a loyal minister and a devoted son. Where lies his offense?

sentences.chinese: 尹僕射棄先王之典，而欲遵漢、魏之權制，豈所望於朝賢哉！
sentences.literal: Director Yin casts aside the canons of the former kings yet wishes to follow Han and Wei's expedient regulations—is this what is expected of court worthies!
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Director Yin Wei would discard the models of the ancient kings and cling to the expedients of Han and Wei—is that what we expect of worthy ministers?

sentences.chinese: 其一依嵩議。」
sentences.literal: In all matters follow Song's proposal.
sentences.idiomatic: Let everything be decided according to Li Song's memorial.

sentences.chinese: 鮮卑薛勃叛奔嶺北，上郡、貳川雜胡皆應之，遂圍安遠將軍姚詳于金城。
sentences.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled and fled north of the ranges; the miscellaneous Hu of Shangjun and Erchuan all responded; thereupon they besieged Yao Xiang the General Who Pacifies the Distance at Jincheng.
sentences.idiomatic: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled and fled beyond the northern ranges; mixed Hu peoples of Shang Commandery and the Er River basin rose with him, and together they besieged Yao Xiang, General Who Pacifies the Distance, at Jincheng.

sentences.chinese: 遣姚崇、尹緯討之。
sentences.literal: He sent Yao Chong and Yin Wei to attack them.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yao Chong and Yin Wei to suppress the revolt.

sentences.chinese: 勃自三交趣金城，崇列營掎之，而租運不繼，三軍大饑。
sentences.literal: Bo hurried from Sanjiao toward Jincheng; Chong arrayed camps to pin him, but grain transport did not continue and the three armies starved greatly.
sentences.idiomatic: Xue Bo drove from Sanjiao toward Jincheng; Yao Chong drew up camps to contain him, yet supplies failed to arrive and the entire army faced famine.

sentences.chinese: 緯言於崇曰：「輔國彌姐高地、建節杜成等皆諸部之豪，位班三品，督運稽留，令三軍乏絕，宜明置刑書，以懲不肅。
sentences.literal: Wei said to Chong: "Mijie Gaodi who Supports the State, Du Cheng who Establishes Integrity, and others are magnates of the various tribes, ranked third grade; they supervised transport and delayed, causing the three armies to lack supplies—clear punishment should be applied to warn against lack of discipline.
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei told Yao Chong: "Mijie Gaodi, the general who supports the state, Du Cheng, who holds the banner of integrity, and others are tribal chiefs of third-rank standing. They were charged with convoys yet stalled them until the army ran dry. Apply the penal code openly to restore discipline.

sentences.chinese: 」遂斬之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon they executed them.
sentences.idiomatic: They executed the negligent officers.

sentences.chinese: 諸部大震，租入者五十餘萬。
sentences.literal: The tribes were greatly shaken; grain contributions exceeded five hundred thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: The tribal levies were terrified into compliance, and more than five hundred thousand measures of grain poured in.

sentences.chinese: 興率步騎二萬親討之，勃懼，棄其眾奔于高平公沒奕于，於執而送之。
sentences.literal: Xing led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry personally to attack him; Bo feared, abandoned his host and fled to the Duke of Gaoping Moyuyu; Yu seized him and sent him in.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing personally led twenty thousand foot and horse against him; Xue Bo panicked, abandoned his troops, and fled to Moyuyu, Duke of Gaoping, who seized him and handed him over to Yao Xing.

sentences.chinese: 泫氏男姚買得欲因興葬母虵氏殺興，會有告之者，興未之信，遣李嵩詐往。
sentences.literal: Yao Maide, Baron of Xuanshi, wished to take advantage of Xing burying mother Lady She to kill Xing; someone informed on him; Xing did not believe it and sent Li Song feigning (a visit).
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Maide, a baron of Xuanshi county, plotted to murder Yao Xing during the burial of Lady She. When an informer brought word, Yao Xing doubted the tale and sent Li Song on a pretended errand to probe the matter.

sentences.chinese: 買得具以告嵩，嵩還，以聞，興乃賜買得死，誅其黨與。
sentences.literal: Maide fully told Song; Song returned and reported; Xing then granted Maide death and executed his associates.
sentences.idiomatic: Maide confessed everything to Li Song, who reported back; Yao Xing then forced Maide to take his own life and executed his accomplices.

sentences.chinese: 興下書禁百姓造錦繡及淫祀。
sentences.literal: Xing issued an edict forbidding the common people from making brocades and excessive sacrifices.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing promulgated an edict forbidding commoners to weave brocades and to practice illicit, excessive worship.

sentences.chinese: 興率眾寇湖城，晉弘農太守陶仲山、華山太守董邁皆降於興。
sentences.literal: Xing led the host to raid Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan Administrator of Hongnong for Jin and Dong Mai Administrator of Huashan both surrendered to Xing.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing led his army against Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan, Eastern Jin's Administrator of Hongnong, and Dong Mai, Administrator of Huashan, both capitulated.

sentences.chinese: 遂如陝城，進寇上洛，陷之。
sentences.literal: Thereupon he went to Shancheng, advanced to raid Shangluo, and took it.
sentences.idiomatic: He then advanced to Shancheng, struck Shangluo, and captured the city.

sentences.chinese: 遣姚崇寇洛陽，晉河南太守夏侯宗之固守金墉，崇攻之不克，乃陷柏穀，徙流人西河嚴彥、河東裴岐、韓襲等二萬餘戶而還。
sentences.literal: He sent Yao Chong to raid Luoyang; Xiahou Zongzhi Administrator of Henan for Jin firmly held Jinyong; Chong attacked without success, then took Bogu, and relocated the displaced households of Yan Yan from Xihe, Pei Qi and Han Xi from Hedong—more than twenty thousand households—and returned.
sentences.idiomatic: He sent Yao Chong against Luoyang; Xiahou Zongzhi, Jin's Administrator of Henan, held the Jinyong fortress and repelled him, so Yao Chong turned aside, seized Bogu, and marched away more than twenty thousand displaced households led by Yan Yan of Xihe and Pei Qi and Han Xi of Hedong.

sentences.chinese: 興下書，令士卒戰亡者守宰所在埋藏之，求其近親為之立後。
sentences.literal: Xing issued an edict ordering that soldiers who died in battle be buried where local officials were; their close kin were sought to establish heirs for them.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing issued an edict requiring local magistrates to bury soldiers fallen in battle within their jurisdictions and to find close kin to continue each man's line.

sentences.chinese: 武都氐屠飛、啖鐵等殺隴東太守姚回，略三千餘家，據方山以叛。
sentences.literal: The Wu Du Di Tu Fei, Dan Tie, and others killed Yao Hui Administrator of Longdong, plundered more than three thousand households, and held Fangshan in rebellion.
sentences.idiomatic: Tu Fei, Dan Tie, and other Di leaders from Wudu murdered Yao Hui, Administrator of Longdong, ravaged more than three thousand households, and entrenched themselves on Fangshan in rebellion.

sentences.chinese: 興遣姚紹等討之，斬飛、鐵。
sentences.literal: Xing sent Yao Shao and others to attack them and beheaded Fei and Tie.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Yao Shao and others against them and executed Tu Fei and Dan Tie.

sentences.chinese: 遣狄伯支迎流人曹會、牛壽萬餘戶於漢中。
sentences.literal: He sent Di Bozhi to welcome the displaced households of Cao Hui and Niu Shou—more than ten thousand households—from Hanzhong.
sentences.idiomatic: He dispatched Di Bozhi to escort more than ten thousand displaced households led by Cao Hui and Niu Shou out of Hanzhong.

sentences.chinese: 興留心政事，苞容廣納，一言之善，咸見禮異。
sentences.literal: Xing attended to government affairs, embraced and tolerated broadly; any good word was treated with special courtesy.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing devoted himself to governance, generous in tolerance and eager for counsel; even a single sound suggestion earned distinctive honor.

sentences.chinese: 京兆杜瑾、馮翊吉默、始平周寶等上陳時事，皆擢處美官。
sentences.literal: Du Jin of Jingzhao, Ji Mo of Fengyi, Zhou Bao of Shiping, and others submitted analyses of current affairs; all were promoted to fine offices.
sentences.idiomatic: Du Jin of Jingzhao, Ji Mo of Fengyi, Zhou Bao of Shiping, and others memorialized on policy; each was promoted to a prestigious post.

sentences.chinese: 天水姜龕、東平淳于岐、馮翊郭高等皆耆儒碩德，經明行修，各門徒數百，教授長安，諸生自遠而至者萬數千人。
sentences.literal: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were aged scholars of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct; each had hundreds of disciples and taught in Chang'an; students coming from afar numbered ten thousand or more.
sentences.idiomatic: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were eminent elder scholars, masters of the classics and models of conduct; each commanded hundreds of disciples and lectured in Chang'an, while learners arrived from distant regions by the tens of thousands.

sentences.chinese: 興每於聽政之暇，引龕等於東堂，講論道藝，錯綜名理。
sentences.literal: Xing often in the leisure after hearing cases summoned Kan and others to the eastern hall to lecture on the Way and arts, weaving together names and principles.
sentences.idiomatic: Whenever court business allowed, Yao Xing invited Jiang Kan and his peers to the eastern hall to debate learning and sort through philosophical distinctions.

sentences.chinese: 涼州胡辯，苻堅之末，東徙洛陽，講授弟子千有餘人，關中後進多赴之請業。
sentences.literal: Hu Bian of Liangzhou, at the end of Fu Jian's reign, moved east to Luoyang and taught more than a thousand disciples; many younger scholars from Guanzhong went to seek instruction.
sentences.idiomatic: Hu Bian of Liangzhou had relocated east to Luoyang near the end of Fu Jian's rule; he instructed over a thousand pupils, and ambitious young scholars from Guanzhong flocked to study under him.

sentences.chinese: 興敕關尉曰：「諸生諮訪道藝，修己厲身，往來出入，勿拘常限。
sentences.literal: Xing instructed the gate captain: "Students who inquire into the Way and arts and cultivate themselves—coming and going—do not restrain by usual limits.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing ordered the frontier captains: "Students who pursue learning and cultivate their characters may pass the checkpoints without the usual curfew restrictions.

sentences.chinese: 」於是學者咸勸，儒風盛焉。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon scholars were all encouraged and Confucian culture flourished.
sentences.idiomatic: Scholars took fresh heart, and Confucian learning flourished as never before.

sentences.chinese: 給事黃門侍郎古成詵、中書侍郎王尚、尚書郎馬岱等，以文章雅正，參管機密。
sentences.literal: Gucheng Shen, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; Ma Dai, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; and others, by elegant and upright composition, took part in confidential government.
sentences.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; Ma Dai, Gentleman at the Masters of Writing; and others—writers of refined, principled prose—were admitted to confidential deliberations.

sentences.chinese: 詵風韻秀舉，確然不群，每以天下是非為己任。
sentences.literal: Shen's bearing was refined and elevated, assuredly not of the common herd; he always took the rights and wrongs of all under Heaven as his responsibility.
sentences.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen carried himself with poised distinction; he stood apart from the crowd and habitually treated the moral welfare of the empire as his personal charge.

sentences.chinese: 時京兆韋高慕阮籍之為人，居母喪，彈琴飲酒。
sentences.literal: At the time Wei Gao of Jingzhao admired Ruan Ji's conduct; during mourning for his mother he played zither and drank wine.
sentences.idiomatic: At that time Wei Gao of Jingzhao, emulating Ruan Ji, played the zither and drank wine while mourning his mother.

sentences.chinese: 詵聞而泣曰：「吾當私刃斬之，以崇風教。
sentences.literal: Shen heard and wept, saying: "I ought to cut him down with a private blade to exalt custom and instruction.
sentences.idiomatic: When Gucheng Shen heard of it, he wept and swore, "I should run him through with my own sword for the sake of public morality.

sentences.chinese: 」遂持劍求高。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he took a sword and sought Gao.
sentences.idiomatic: He seized a blade and went looking for Wei Gao.

sentences.chinese: 高懼，逃匿，終身不敢見詵。
sentences.literal: Gao feared, fled and hid, and to the end of his life dared not meet Shen.
sentences.idiomatic: Terrified, Wei Gao fled into hiding and never again dared face Gucheng Shen.

sentences.chinese: 興遣將鎮東楊佛嵩攻陷洛陽。
sentences.literal: Xing sent the general Yang Fosong who Stabilizes the East to attack and take Luoyang.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yang Fosong, General Who Stabilizes the East, who captured Luoyang.
